sanskrit: aparāhṇe parāhṇasya sūtaputrasya māriṣa chinnam añjalikenājau sotsedham apatac chiraḥ
english: In the late afternoon following midday, O honored one, the head of the Sūtaputra, severed in battle by the añjalika arrow, fell to the earth high-crested.

sanskrit: upary upari sainyānāṃ tasya śatros tad añjasā śiraḥ karṇasya sotsedham iṣuḥ so 'pāharad drutam
english: That arrow swiftly bore away, high over the heads of the armies, the lofty head of his foe Karṇa, carrying it straight on.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇaṃ tu śūraṃ patitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; śarācitaṃ śoṇitadigdhagātram dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ bhuvi madrarājaś; chinnadhvajenāpayayau rathena
english: Saṃjaya said: But when the king of the Madras saw the hero Karṇa fallen upon the earth, studded with arrows, his limbs smeared with blood, lying upon the ground, he withdrew with his chariot, its banner cut away.

sanskrit: karṇe hate kuravaḥ prādravanta; bhayārditā gāḍhaviddhāś ca saṃkhye avekṣamāṇā muhur arjunasya; dhvajaṃ mahāntaṃ vapuṣā jvalantam
english: When Karṇa was slain, the Kurus fled, tormented by fear and deeply wounded in the fray, glancing again and again at the great banner of Arjuna, blazing with its form.

sanskrit: sahasranetrapratimānakarmaṇaḥ; sahasrapatrapratimānanaṃ śubham sahasraraśmir dinasaṃkṣaye yathā; tathāpatat tasya śiro vasuṃdharām
english: As the thousand-rayed sun sinks at the close of day, so fell to the earth the fair head of him whose deeds rivaled the thousand-eyed Indra, whose face was like the thousand-petaled lotus.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śalyas tu karṇārjunayor vimarde; balāni dṛṣṭvā mṛditāni bāṇaiḥ duryodhanaṃ yāntam avekṣamāṇo; saṃdarśayad bhārata yuddhabhūmim
english: Saṃjaya said: But Śalya, seeing the armies ground down by the arrows in the clash of Karṇa and Arjuna, and watching Duryodhana as he came on, showed him the field of battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nipātitasyandanavājināgaṃ; dṛṣṭvā balaṃ tad dhatasūtaputram duryodhano 'śrupratipūrṇanetro; muhur muhur nyaśvasad ārtarūpaḥ
english: Beholding that host with its chariots, horses, and elephants struck down, and the Sūtaputra slain, Duryodhana, his eyes brimming with tears, sighed again and again, his form stricken with grief.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ tu śūraṃ patitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; śarācitaṃ śoṇitadigdhagātram yadṛcchayā sūryam ivāvanisthaṃ; didṛkṣavaḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ
english: And around the hero Karṇa, fallen upon the earth, studded with arrows, his limbs smeared with blood, like the sun by some chance brought down to the ground, they stood encircling him, eager to gaze upon him.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭavitrastaviṣaṇṇavismṛtās; tathāpare śokagatā ivābhavan pare tvadīyāś ca paraspareṇa; yathā yathaiṣāṃ prakṛtis tathābhavan
english: Some were elated, some terrified, some despondent, some bewildered, and others as if sunk in grief; both your foes and your own men became, each toward the other, just as their nature was.

sanskrit: praviddhavarmābharaṇāmbarāyudhaṃ; dhanaṃjayenābhihataṃ hataujasam niśamya karṇaṃ kuravaḥ pradudruvur; hatarṣabhā gāva ivākulākulāḥ
english: Seeing Karṇa, his armor, ornaments, garments, and weapons scattered, struck down by Dhanaṃjaya and his vigor destroyed, the Kurus fled in utter confusion, like cattle whose bull has been slain.

sanskrit: kṛtvā vimardaṃ bhṛśam arjunena; karṇaṃ hataṃ kesariṇeva nāgam dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ bhuvi madrarājo; bhīto 'pasarpat sarathaḥ suśīghram
english: Having waged a fierce struggle with Arjuna, when the king of the Madras saw Karṇa slain and lying upon the ground—like an elephant felled by a lion—he, afraid, withdrew with his chariot in all haste.

sanskrit: madrādhipaś cāpi vimūḍhacetās; tūrṇaṃ rathenāpahṛtadhvajena duryodhanasyāntikam etya śīghraṃ; saṃbhāṣya duḥkhārtam uvāca vākyam
english: And the lord of the Madras, his mind bewildered, came swiftly upon his chariot whose banner had been carried off to the side of Duryodhana, and addressing him, stricken with sorrow, spoke these words.

sanskrit: viśīrṇanāgāśvarathapravīraṃ; balaṃ tvadiyaṃ yamarāṣṭrakalpam anyonyam āsādya hataṃ mahadbhir; narāśvanāgair girikūṭakalpaiḥ
english: Your host, its elephants, horses, chariots, and champions shattered, has become like the realm of Yama, slain as they met one another in combat by mighty men, horses, and elephants vast as mountain peaks.

sanskrit: naitādṛśaṃ bhārata yuddham āsīd; yathādya karṇārjunayor babhūva grastau hi karṇena sametya kṛṣṇāv; anye ca sarve tava śatravo ye
english: Never, O Bhārata, has there been such a battle as today was waged between Karṇa and Arjuna; for Karṇa, closing in, had seized both the Kṛṣṇas and all the rest of those who were your foes.

sanskrit: daivaṃ tu yat tat svavaśaṃ pravṛttaṃ; tat pāṇḍavān pāti hinasti cāsmān tavārthasiddhyarthakarā hi sarve; prasahya vīrā nihatā dviṣadbhiḥ
english: But that Fate which moves of its own power protects the Pāṇḍavas and destroys us; for all those heroes who labored to achieve your purpose have been overpowered and slain by the enemy.

sanskrit: kuberavaivasvatavāsavānāṃ; tulyaprabhāvāmbupateś ca vīrāḥ vīryeṇa śauryeṇa balena caiva; tais taiś ca yuktā vipulair guṇaughaiḥ
english: Heroes equal in might to Kubera, to Yama the son of Vivasvat, to Vāsava, and to Varuṇa the lord of waters—endowed with valor, with prowess, with strength, and with whole floods of manifold virtues—

sanskrit: avadhyakalpā nihatā narendrās; tavārthakāmā yudhi pāṇḍaveyaiḥ tan mā śuco bhārata diṣṭam etat; paryāyasiddhir na sadāsti siddhiḥ
english: those kings, well-nigh unslayable, who sought your welfare, have been slain in battle by the sons of Pāṇḍu. Grieve not for this, O Bhārata; this is destiny. Success comes by turns; it is not forever assured.

sanskrit: etad vaco madrapater niśamya; svaṃ cāpanītaṃ manasā nirīkṣya duryodhano dīnamanā visaṃjñaḥ; punaḥ punar nyaśvasad ārtarūpaḥ
english: Hearing these words of the lord of the Madras, and surveying in his mind his own misconduct, Duryodhana, his spirit broken and his senses gone, sighed again and again, his form stricken with grief.

sanskrit: taṃ dhyānamūkaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ bhṛśārtam; ārtāyanir dīnam uvāca vākyam paśyedam ugraṃ naravājināgair; āyodhanaṃ vīrahataiḥ prapannam
english: To him, mute with brooding, pitiable, sorely stricken and wretched, the son of Ārtāyana spoke these words: "Behold this dreadful battlefield, strewn with men, horses, and elephants, and with slain heroes.

sanskrit: mahīdharābhaiḥ patitair mahāgajaiḥ; sakṛt praviddhaiḥ śaraviddhamarmabhiḥ tair vihvaladbhiś ca gatāsubhiś ca; pradhvastayantrāyudhavarmayodhaiḥ
english: With great elephants like mountains, fallen, flung down at a single stroke, their vital parts pierced by arrows—some of them writhing, others lifeless—their drivers, weapons, armor, and warriors all shattered;

sanskrit: vajrāpaviddhair iva cācalendrair; vibhinnapāṣāṇamṛgadrumauṣadhaiḥ praviddhaghaṇṭāṅkuśatomaradhvajaiḥ; sahemamālai rudhiraughasaṃplutaiḥ
english: like lordly mountains shattered by the thunderbolt, their rocks, beasts, trees, and herbs broken apart—their bells, goads, lances, and banners flung away, garlanded with gold and drenched in floods of blood;

sanskrit: śarāvabhinnaiḥ patitaiś ca vājibhiḥ; śvasadbhir anyaiḥ kṣatajaṃ vamadbhiḥ dīnaiḥ stanadbhiḥ parivṛttanetrair; mahīṃ daśadbhiḥ kṛpaṇaṃ nadadbhiḥ
english: with horses pierced by arrows and fallen, some still breathing, others vomiting blood, wretched and groaning, their eyes rolling, biting the earth and crying out piteously;

sanskrit: tathāpaviddhair gajavājiyodhair; mandāsubhiś caiva gatāsubhiś ca narāśvanāgaiś ca rathaiś ca marditair; mahī mahāvaitaraṇīva durdṛśā
english: with elephant-warriors and horsemen flung down, some with breath ebbing, others lifeless—with men, horses, elephants, and chariots all crushed, the earth is grim to look upon, like the great Vaitaraṇī river of death.

sanskrit: gajair nikṛttāparahastagātrair; udvepamānaiḥ patitaiḥ pṛthivyām yaśasvibhir nāgarathāśvayodhibhiḥ; padātibhiś cābhimukhair hataiḥ paraiḥ viśīrṇavarmābharaṇāmbarāyudhair; vṛtā niśāntair iva pāvakair mahī
english: With elephants their trunks and limbs lopped off, shuddering as they fell to the earth; with glorious elephant-, chariot-, and horse-warriors, and with foot-soldiers, the enemies who fell facing the foe—their armor, ornaments, garments, and weapons scattered—the earth lies covered, as though strewn with fires burnt out at dawn.

sanskrit: śaraprahārābhihatair mahābalair; avekṣyamāṇaiḥ patitaiḥ sahasraśaḥ pranaṣṭasaṃjñaiḥ punar ucchvasadbhir; mahī babhūvānugatair ivāgnibhiḥ divaś cyutair bhūr atidīptimadbhir; naktaṃ grahair dyaur amaleva dīptaiḥ
english: With mighty men struck down by arrow-strokes, gazed upon as they lay fallen by the thousand—their senses lost, then breathing once more—the earth seemed as if pervaded by fires; the ground shone as if strewn with planets fallen from heaven and blazing bright, like a clear night-sky aflame with stars.

sanskrit: śarās tu karṇārjunabāhumuktā; vidārya nāgāśvamanuṣyadehān prāṇān nirasyāśu mahīm atīyur; mahoragā vāsam ivābhito 'straiḥ
english: The arrows loosed from the arms of Karṇa and Arjuna, tearing through the bodies of elephants, horses, and men and swiftly casting out their life-breaths, entered the earth, like great serpents seeking their lairs on every side.

sanskrit: hatair manuṣyāśvagajaiś ca saṃkhye; śarāvabhinnaiś ca rathair babhūva dhanaṃjayasyādhiratheś ca mārge; gajair agamyā vasudhātidurgā
english: With men, horses, and elephants slain in the fray, and chariots shattered by arrows, the ground along the path of Dhanaṃjaya and the son of Adhiratha became impassable even for elephants, exceedingly hard to traverse.

sanskrit: rathair vareṣūn mathitaiś ca yodhaiḥ; saṃsyūtasūtāśvavarāyudhadhvajaiḥ viśīrṇaśastrair vinikṛttabandhurair; nikṛttacakrākṣayugatriveṇubhiḥ
english: With chariots, and warriors mangled by choice shafts, their drivers, horses, fine weapons, and banners pierced through, their arms scattered, their seats hewn apart, their wheels, axles, yokes, and triple-poles cut to pieces;

sanskrit: vimuktayantrair nihatair ayasmayair; hatānuṣaṅgair viniṣaṅgabandhuraiḥ prabhagnanīḍair maṇihemamaṇḍitaiḥ; stṛtā mahī dyaur iva śāradair ghanaiḥ
english: with their gear torn loose, their iron fittings broken, their appendages destroyed, their quivers and frames split, their bodies shattered though adorned with gems and gold—the earth lay strewn with them, like the sky with autumn clouds.

sanskrit: vikṛṣyamaṇair javanair alaṃkṛtair; hateśvarair ājirathaiḥ sukalpitaiḥ manuṣyamātaṅgarathāśvarāśibhir; drutaṃ vrajanto bahudhā vicūrṇitāḥ
english: By heaps of men, elephants, chariots, and horses, war-chariots well-fashioned, swift and adorned, their drivers slain—as they rushed swiftly on, dragged along—were ground to powder in manifold ways.

sanskrit: sahemapaṭṭāḥ parighāḥ paraśvadhāḥ; kaḍaṅgarāyomusalāni paṭṭiśāḥ petuś ca khaḍgā vimalā vikośā; gadāś ca jāmbūnadapaṭṭabaddhāḥ
english: Iron bludgeons banded with gold, battle-axes, spiked iron clubs, pestles, and pikes; and spotless swords drawn from their sheaths; and maces bound with bands of refined gold—all these had fallen.

sanskrit: cāpāni rukmāṅgadabhūṣaṇāni; śarāś ca kārtasvaracitrapuṅkhāḥ ṛṣṭyaś ca pītā vimalā vikośāḥ; prāsāḥ sakhaḍgāḥ kanakāvabhāsāḥ
english: Bows adorned with golden armlets and ornaments; arrows with shafts bright with gold; gleaming, spotless rapiers drawn from their scabbards; and javelins with swords, all shining like gold;

sanskrit: chatrāṇi vālavyajanāni śaṅkhāḥ; srajaś ca puṣpottamahemacitrāḥ kuthāḥ patākāmbaraveṣṭitāś ca; kirīṭamālā mukuṭāś ca śubhrāḥ
english: Parasols, yak-tail fans, conches, and garlands bright with the choicest flowers and gold; elephant-housings wrapped in banner-cloths; diadem-wreaths and gleaming crowns;

sanskrit: prakīrṇakā viprakīrṇāḥ kuthāś ca; pradhānamuktātaralāś ca hārāḥ āpīḍakeyūravarāṅgadāni; graiveyaniṣkāḥ sasuvarṇasūtrāḥ
english: Whisks scattered about, and housings, and necklaces with quivering pendants of choicest pearls; head-ornaments, armlets, and fine bracelets; neck-chains and golden ornaments strung on threads of gold;

sanskrit: maṇyuttamā vajrasuvarṇamuktā; ratnāni coccāvacamaṅgalāni gātrāṇi cātyantasukhocitāni; śirāṃsi cendupratimānanāni
english: finest gems, diamonds, gold, and pearls, and auspicious jewels both great and small; bodies long accustomed to the utmost ease, and heads whose faces were like the moon;

sanskrit: dehāṃś ca bhogāṃś ca paricchadāṃś ca; tyaktvā manojñāni sukhāni cāpi svadharmaniṣṭhāṃ mahatīm avāpya; vyāptāṃś ca lokān yaśasā samīyuḥ
english: Forsaking their bodies, their enjoyments, their possessions, and all that was delightful and pleasant, and attaining a great steadfastness in their own duty, they passed to the worlds that they had filled with their fame.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā virarāma śalyo; duryodhanaḥ śokaparītacetāḥ hā karṇa hā karṇa iti bruvāṇa; ārto visaṃjño bhṛśam aśrunetraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Śalya fell silent; and Duryodhana, his mind beset with grief, crying "Alas, Karṇa! Alas, Karṇa!", was stricken, bereft of his senses, his eyes streaming with tears.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaputrapramukhā narendrāḥ; sarve samāśvāsya saha prayānti nirīkṣamāṇā muhur arjunasya; dhvajaṃ mahāntaṃ yaśasā jvalantam
english: All the kings, with the son of Droṇa at their head, comforted him and went on together, glancing again and again at the great banner of Arjuna, blazing with glory.

sanskrit: narāśvamātaṅgaśarīrajena; raktena siktā rudhireṇa bhūmiḥ raktāmbarasrak tapanīyayogān; nārī prakāśā iva sarvagamyā
english: The earth, drenched red with the blood streaming from the bodies of men, horses, and elephants, shone like a woman robed and garlanded in red, gleaming with gold—open to the approach of all.

sanskrit: pracchannarūpā rudhireṇa rājan; raudre muhūrte 'tivirājamānāḥ naivāvatasthuḥ kuravaḥ samīkṣya; pravrājitā devalokāś ca sarve
english: Their forms hidden by blood, O king, shining brightly in that dreadful hour, the Kurus could not stand their ground when they looked upon it; all were driven forth, as if banished from the worlds of the gods.

sanskrit: vadhena karṇasya suduḥkhitās te; hā karṇa hā karṇa iti bruvāṇāḥ drutaṃ prayātāḥ śibirāṇi rājan; divākaraṃ raktam avekṣamāṇāḥ
english: Sorely grieved by the slaying of Karṇa, crying "Alas, Karṇa! Alas, Karṇa!", they hastened swiftly to their camps, O king, gazing upon the reddened sun.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvamuktais tu suvarṇapuṅkhaiḥ; śitaiḥ śaraiḥ śoṇitadigdhavājaiḥ śaraiś citāṅgo bhuvi bhāti karṇo; hato 'pi san sūrya ivāṃśumālī
english: His body studded with the keen, gold-shafted arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, their feathers smeared with blood, Karṇa shone upon the earth, slain though he was, like the sun wreathed in its rays.

sanskrit: karṇasya dehaṃ rudhirāvasiktaṃ; bhaktānukampī bhagavān vivasvān spṛṣṭvā karair lohitaraktarūpaḥ; siṣṇāsur abhyeti paraṃ samudram
english: The blessed Vivasvat, compassionate to his devotee, touching with his rays the blood-drenched body of Karṇa and taking on a deep red hue, drew near to the far ocean as if longing to bathe.

sanskrit: itīva saṃcintya surarṣisaṃghāḥ; saṃprasthitā yānti yathāniketam saṃcintayitvā ca janā visasrur; yathāsukhaṃ khaṃ ca mahītalaṃ ca
english: Reflecting thus, the hosts of gods and sages set out and went, each to his own abode; and the people too, having pondered, dispersed at their ease across the sky and the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ bhayaṃkaraṃ; niśamya yuddhaṃ kuruvīramukhyayoḥ dhanaṃjayasyādhiratheś ca vismitāḥ; praśaṃsamānāḥ prayayus tadā janāḥ
english: Having witnessed that wondrous battle of the foremost Kuru heroes, terrible to all living things—the battle of Dhanaṃjaya and the son of Adhiratha—the people, marveling and full of praise, then went their way.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ saṃkṛttavarmāṇaṃ vīraṃ viśasane hatam gatāsum api rādheyaṃ naiva lakṣmīr vyamuñcata
english: Though the hero Rādheya, his armor cut through by arrows, slain in the slaughter, had given up his life, yet his beauty did not forsake him even then.

sanskrit: nānābharaṇavān rājan mṛṣṭajāmbūnadāṅgadaḥ hato vaikartanaḥ śete pādapo 'ṅkuravān iva
english: Adorned with manifold ornaments, O king, his armlets of burnished gold, the slain Vaikartana lay like a tree in blossom.

sanskrit: kanakottamasaṃkāśaḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ saputraḥ puruṣavyāghraḥ saṃśāntaḥ pārthatejasā pratāpya pāṇḍavān rājan pāñcālāṃś cāstratejasā
english: Bright as the finest gold, like a blazing fire, that tiger among men, with his son, was quenched by the splendor of Pārtha, O king—he who had scorched the Pāṇḍavas and the Pāñcālas with the fire of his weapons.

sanskrit: dadānīty eva yo 'vocan na nāstīty arthito 'rthibhiḥ sadbhiḥ sadā satpuruṣaḥ sa hato dvairathe vṛṣaḥ
english: He who, ever a good man among the good, when entreated by suppliants would say "I shall give," and never "There is none"—that bull among men was slain in single chariot-combat.

sanskrit: yasya brāhmaṇasāt sarvam ātmārthaṃ na mahātmanaḥ nādeyaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv āsīd yasya svam api jīvitam
english: For that great-souled one, all was bestowed upon the brāhmaṇas, nothing kept for himself; there was nothing he would not give to the brāhmaṇas—not even his own life.

sanskrit: sadā nṝṇāṃ priyo dātā priyadāno divaṃ gataḥ ādāya tava putrāṇāṃ jayāśāṃ śarma varma ca
english: Ever dear to men, a giver whose gifts were dear, he has gone to heaven, bearing away the hope of victory of your sons, their refuge and their shield.

sanskrit: hate sma karṇe sarito na sravanti; jagāma cāstaṃ kaluṣo divākaraḥ grahaś ca tiryag jvalitārkavarṇo; yamasya putro 'bhyudiyāya rājan
english: When Karṇa was slain, the rivers ceased to flow; the sun went down darkened; and the planet that is the son of Yama, glowing aslant with the hue of the burning sun, rose up, O king.

sanskrit: nabhaḥ paphālātha nanāda corvī; vavuś ca vātāḥ paruṣātivelam diśaḥ sadhūmāś ca bhṛśaṃ prajajvalur; mahārṇavāś cukṣubhire ca sasvanāḥ
english: The sky split asunder, and the earth roared; the winds blew harsh beyond all measure; the quarters, wreathed in smoke, blazed fiercely; and the great oceans heaved with a thunderous din.

sanskrit: sakānanāḥ sādricayāś cakampuḥ; pravivyathur bhūtagaṇāś ca māriṣa bṛhaspatī rohiṇīṃ saṃprapīḍya; babhūva candrārkasamānavarṇaḥ
english: The mountains with their forests and their ranges trembled, and the hosts of creatures were sore afflicted, O honored one; and Bṛhaspati, oppressing Rohiṇī, took on a hue like that of the moon and the sun.

sanskrit: hate karṇe na diśo viprajajñus; tamovṛtā dyaur vicacāla bhūmiḥ papāta colkā jvalanaprakāśā; niśācarāś cāpy abhavan prahṛṣṭāḥ
english: When Karṇa was slain, the quarters could not be discerned, veiled in darkness; the heaven shook, the earth quaked; a meteor fell, bright as fire; and the prowlers of the night grew exceedingly glad.

sanskrit: śaśiprakāśānanam arjuno yadā; kṣureṇa karṇasya śiro nyapātayat athāntarikṣe divi ceha cāsakṛd; babhūva hāheti janasya nisvanaḥ
english: When Arjuna struck down with his razor-arrow the head of Karṇa, whose face shone like the moon, then in the firmament, in heaven, and here below, again and again arose the cry "Alas!" from the people.

sanskrit: sa devagandharvamanuṣyapūjitaṃ; nihatya karṇaṃ ripum āhave 'rjunaḥ rarāja pārthaḥ parameṇa tejasā; vṛtraṃ nihatyeva sahasralocanaḥ
english: Having slain in battle his foe Karṇa, honored by gods, gandharvas, and men, Arjuna the son of Pṛthā shone with surpassing splendor, like the thousand-eyed Indra when he had slain Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tato rathenāmbudavṛndanādinā; śarannabhomadhyagabhāskaratviṣā patākinā bhīmaninādaketunā; himenduśaṅkhasphaṭikāvabhāsinā suvarṇamuktāmaṇivajravidrumair; alaṃkṛtenāpratimānaraṃhasā
english: Then upon his chariot—roaring like a mass of thunderclouds, gleaming like the sun at the zenith of the autumn sky, decked with pennons, its standard sounding a terrible note, shining like snow, the moon, conch, and crystal, adorned with gold, pearls, gems, diamonds, and coral, and of matchless speed—

sanskrit: narottamau pāṇḍavakeśimardanāv; udāhitāv agnidivākaropamau raṇājire vītabhayau virejatuḥ; samānayānāv iva viṣṇuvāsavau
english: those two best of men, crushers of the foes of the Pāṇḍavas, exalted and like unto fire and the sun, free from fear, shone upon the field of battle, as though Viṣṇu and Vāsava rode together in one car.

sanskrit: tato dhanurjyātalaneminisvanaiḥ; prasahya kṛtvā ca ripūn hataprabhān saṃsādhayitvaiva kurūñ śaraughaiḥ; kapidhvajaḥ pakṣivaradhvajaś ca prasahya śaṅkhau dhamatuḥ sughoṣau; manāṃsy arīṇām avasādayantau
english: Then with the twang of bowstring, the slap of the palm-guard, and the rumble of chariot-wheels, having forcibly stripped their foes of their luster and overwhelmed the Kurus with floods of arrows, the ape-bannered one and he whose banner bore the king of birds blew their resounding conches with might, casting down the spirits of their enemies.

sanskrit: suvarṇajālāvatatau mahāsvanau; himāvadātau parigṛhya pāṇibhiḥ cucumbatuḥ śaṅkhavarau nṛṇāṃ varau; varānanābhyāṃ yugapac ca dadhmatuḥ
english: Grasping in their hands those finest of conches, overspread with nets of gold, deep-voiced, and white as snow, those best of men set them to their lips—pressed them with their noble mouths—and blew them together as one.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣo devadattasya cobhayoḥ pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ ca dyām apaś cāpy apūrayat
english: The blast of both the Pāñcajanya and the Devadatta filled the earth, the firmament, the heavens, and the waters.

sanskrit: tau śaṅkhaśabdena ninādayantau; vanāni śailān sarito diśaś ca vitrāsayantau tava putrasenāṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ nandayataḥ sma vīrau
english: Those two heroes, making the forests, mountains, rivers, and quarters ring with the sound of their conches, terrifying the army of your sons, gladdened Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayātāḥ kuravo javena; śrutvaiva śaṅkhasvanam īryamāṇam vihāya madrādhipatiṃ patiṃ ca; duryodhanaṃ bhārata bhāratānām
english: Then the Kurus, the moment they heard the rising sound of the conches, fled with speed, abandoning the lord of the Madras and their own lord, Duryodhana, O Bhārata, the lord of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: mahāhave taṃ bahu śobhamānaṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ bhūtagaṇāḥ sametāḥ tadānvamodanta janārdanaṃ ca; prabhākarāv abhyuditau yathaiva
english: In that great battle the assembled hosts of beings then applauded Dhanaṃjaya, resplendent in his glory, and Janārdana too, as men hail the two luminaries newly risen.

sanskrit: samācitau karṇaśaraiḥ paraṃtapāv; ubhau vyabhātāṃ samare 'cyutārjunau tamo nihatyābhyuditau yathāmalau; śaśāṅkasūryāv iva raśmimālinau
english: Both those scorchers of foes, Acyuta and Arjuna, studded with Karṇa's arrows, shone upon the field, like the spotless moon and sun newly risen, wreathed in their rays, having scattered the darkness.

sanskrit: vihāya tān bāṇagaṇān athāgatau; suhṛdvṛtāv apratimānavikramau sukhaṃ praviṣṭau śibiraṃ svam īśvarau; sadasyahūtāv iva vāsavācyutau
english: Then, casting off those swarms of arrows, the two lords of matchless valor, surrounded by their friends, returned and entered their own camp at ease, like Vāsava and Acyuta summoned to a sacrificial assembly.

sanskrit: sadevagandharvamanuṣyacāraṇair; maharṣibhir yakṣamahoragair api jayābhivṛddhyā parayābhipūjitau; nihatya karṇaṃ paramāhave tadā
english: By gods, gandharvas, men, and cāraṇas, by great sages, yakṣas, and mighty serpents, they were honored with the highest exaltation of victory, having slain Karṇa then in that supreme battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā nipātite karṇe tava sainye ca vidrute āśliṣya pārthaṃ dāśārho harṣād vacanam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: When Karṇa had thus been struck down and your army had fled, the lord of the Dāśārhas embraced Pārtha and out of joy spoke these words.

sanskrit: hato balabhidā vṛtras tvayā karṇo dhanaṃjaya vadhaṃ vai karṇavṛtrābhyāṃ kathayiṣyanti mānavāḥ
english: "Vṛtra was slain by the cleaver of strongholds; Karṇa has been slain by you, O Dhanaṃjaya. Men will tell of these slayings, of Karṇa and of Vṛtra together.

sanskrit: vajriṇā nihato vṛtraḥ saṃyuge bhūritejasā tvayā tu nihataḥ karṇo dhanuṣā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Vṛtra was slain in battle by the wielder of the thunderbolt of vast splendor; but Karṇa was slain by you with your bow and sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tam imaṃ vikramaṃ loke prathitaṃ te yaśovaham nivedayāvaḥ kaunteya dharmarājāya dhīmate
english: This valor of yours, renowned in the world and bearing your fame, let us proclaim, O son of Kuntī, to the wise King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: vadhaṃ karṇasya saṃgrāme dīrghakālacikīrṣitam nivedya dharmarājasya tvam ānṛṇyaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: By announcing to the King of Righteousness the slaying of Karṇa in battle—long desired through all this time—you shall be freed of your debt."

sanskrit: tathety ukte keśavas tu pārthena yadupuṅgavaḥ paryavartayad avyagro rathaṃ rathavarasya tam
english: When Pārtha had said "So be it," Keśava, that bull of the Yadus, calmly turned about the chariot of that foremost of charioteers.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ yudhāmanyuṃ mādrīputrau vṛkodaram yuyudhānaṃ ca govinda idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To Dhṛṣṭadyumna, to Yudhāmanyu, to the two sons of Mādrī, to Vṛkodara, and to Yuyudhāna, Govinda spoke these words.

sanskrit: parān abhimukhā yattās tiṣṭhadhvaṃ bhadram astu vaḥ yāvad āvedyate rājñe hataḥ karṇo 'rjunena vai
english: "Stand watchful, facing the foe—may it be well with you—until it is announced to the king that Karṇa has indeed been slain by Arjuna."

sanskrit: sa taiḥ śūrair anujñāto yayau rājaniveśanam pārtham ādāya govindo dadarśa ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Granted leave by those heroes, Govinda, taking Pārtha with him, went to the king's quarters and beheld Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ rājaśārdūlaṃ kāñcane śayanottame agṛhṇītāṃ ca caraṇau muditau pārthivasya tau
english: That tiger among kings lay upon a splendid golden couch; and the two of them, rejoicing, clasped the feet of the monarch.

sanskrit: tayoḥ praharṣam ālakṣya prahārāṃś cātimānuṣān rādheyaṃ nihataṃ matvā samuttasthau yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Marking their great delight and the marks of their superhuman blows, and judging that Rādheya had been slain, Yudhiṣṭhira rose up.

sanskrit: tato 'smai tad yathāvṛttaṃ vāsudevaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ kathayām āsa karṇasya nidhanaṃ yadunandanaḥ
english: Then Vāsudeva, the delight of the Yadus, ever pleasant of speech, related to him the death of Karṇa just as it had come to pass.
